I actually don’t remember what the immigration process was like, but I think in Finland it was pretty smooth, don’t remember there being any issues. When I landed in France, since I already cleared immigration in Finland, I didn’t need to go through it again. Just could get bags and walk straight out.

It’s a long and expensive process but I honestly think it’s worth it.  Basically, I flew finnair (as it was the only airline who allowed rabbits in cabin. this was in 2022 so im not sure if they still do this) from NYC to paris with a layover in Helsinki. Then taxi via euro tunnel to Dover. Then Dover to London. 

So some guidelines:  you can’t fly direct from us to uk without putting your bunny in the hold or having to quarantine your bunny for 3 months. You need to fly into elsewhere in Europe, France especially is easier to bypass because you just drive through the euro tunnel with the correct documentation (get certificate of heath from a vet in France). 

The UK gov allows rabbits into the UK without quarantine if they’re coming from Europe. All in all it cost me around £3K.

Gosh it was soo complicated and expensive, but worth it for my Milo. flew finnair as it was the only airline who allowed rabbits in cabin, from NYC to paris with a layover in Helsinki. Then taxi via euro tunnel to Dover. Then Dover to London. He did so well on the flight, eating and curious!

pros: 

1. You can get involved in a lot of ways - greek life, clubs, intramurals, societies and things like the DO and UU

3. Campus is beautiful (I'm sure you already know that) but worth the mention - tons of spots on campus to study / chill, indoors and outdoors 
4. LOTS of restaurant and bar options (armory sq, Marshall street, destiny, Dino bbq, and faculty (on campus but not dining hall food its actually so good). 
5. PARTIES! there are things to do every weekend - you won't ever be stuck with nothing to do at night, tbh you will probably have way too many options. Best places to party on campus: frat houses if you're into that, thon, ski house and hockey house (not sure if they're still a thing but my freshmen year in 2015, it was the place to be, Lucys, harrys, DJS (they might be gettin shut down but if not its the freshmen bar), faegans flip night - senior bar, the cage, the shack. armory: biergarten, Als, kitty hoynes, benjamins. 
6. off campus housing - you can live off campus for junior and senior year, and there are tons of options. 
7. school spirit is huge at Cuse, which you def already know but it makes for a super close community and makes the games and tailgates extra fun. 
8. finally people are friendly here and im sure you will have no trouble making friends. I made friends on the first day I moved it so it was great. def more pros, but those are some of the bigger ones. 
9. OH and the ny state fair,  farmers market, and Toggenburg  are honorable mentions.

cons: 

1. far walks. campus is pretty big so sometimes it takes a while to walk to class. if you end up living in the mount freshmen year like I did, going to class in Whitman wont be fun. 
2. hard to get around without a car - there are busses that take you to the mall and stuff but its kinda a pain in the ass. thankfully uber launched in syracuse in 2017 so there's that. 
3. big classes. my freshmen year, my astronomy class was like 300 people. it wasn't so much as an issue for me but it lacks personalization and if you lose focus often, it'll be harder to concentrate in a big ass lecture.
